value.notes: MCE's own service-area page confirms San Anselmo as one of Marin County's member communities. PG&E continues to deliver the power and provide billing/customer service.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized statewide budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025 and remains an active program per SGIP's own statewide announcements (most recently dated 2026-07-23). Administered across PG&E's entire distribution territory, which includes San Anselmo/Marin County.
value.eligibility: PG&E, SCE, or SDG&E residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Reused as a utility-level fact already established for other IOU-territory records this session: the CPUC-administered SGIP program applies uniformly across the named utility's entire distribution territory, directly verified via SGIP's own site (selfgenca.com) / the CPUC's own SGIP program page, including a program-status announcement as recent as 2026-07-23 confirming the program remains active.

value: Schedule the inspection online through the eTRAKiT portal once the permit is in Issued status
Select a morning (9:00 a.m.-12:30 p.m.) or afternoon (1:00 p.m.-4:00 p.m.) window
Have the inspection card and Town-stamped plans available on site, with someone present for the full window
Inspection results are typically available in eTrakit the following business day
inspection_steps.notes: This is the Town's general Building Inspections process (the same page covers all building permit types, including solar); the Town's page does not describe a separate, solar-specific inspection sequence.

value.notes: Permit processing takes approximately 1-3 business days, depending on staff availability.

other_conditions: Three permit categories: PV Only Residential, PV with ESS Residential, ESS Only Residential
Contractors must meet PV contractor's license requirements per the CSLB's Solar Smart program
Some applications may be disqualified from using the automated system and require standard review
